newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wool prices improve overall at NZ sales.
newsitem.headline: Wool prices improve overall at NZ sales.

text.p: Overall prices generally improved at wool sales in Napier and Christchurch on Thursday, thanks mainly to an increase in fine and lambswool, Wools of New Zealand said. Crossbred wools generally eased.
The market indicator rose five cents to 426 cents. The fine segment climbed 31 cents to 807, medium rose 41 to 508 and lamb firmed seven to 369, while the strong segment fell seven to 379.

The offering was 41,949 bales, 4,950 tonnes, of which the main components were 42 percent crossbred fleece, 19 percent second shear, 16 percent lambswool and nine percent halfbred. Twenty-four percent was passed in.

Compared with Christchurch on December 19, merino fleece was 3-5 percent dearer, halfbred 24 micron up to 2.5 percent dearer, 25 micron unchanged and 26 and stronger par to one percent cheaper. Compared with Napier and Christchurch last week, crossbred 32-34 micron was 2.5 percent dearer, while 35 and 36 micron was 1.5 percent cheaper and 37 and stronger was up to 3.5 percent cheaper. Cotts were 2-4 percent cheaper, second shear up to 2.5 percent cheaper, and first lambs par to two percent dearer. Second lambs were mixed, bulky skirtings unchanged and second shear bellies and pieces par to 1.5 percent dearer. Main interest came from Western Europe, China, Nepal and local mills.
